name: Suet Dumplings for Soup
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: finely chopped suet
ingredients.originalText: One cup of finely chopped suet

instructions.text: Sift baking powder into the flour
Rub the finely chopped suet well into the flour with the salt
Wet all with sweet milk to make a dough as stiff as biscuit
Make into small balls as large as peaches, well floured
Drop into the soup three-quarters of an hour before being served
Require steady boiling, being closely covered, and the cover not to be removed until taken up to serve

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Sift baking powder into the flour
2. Rub the finely chopped suet well into the flour with the salt
3. Wet all with sweet milk to make a dough as stiff as biscuit
4. Make into small balls as large as peaches, well floured
5. Drop into the soup three-quarters of an hour before being served
6. Require steady boiling, being closely covered, and the cover not to be removed until taken up to serve
